h: Lakes, wildlife and a day by the water
p: The setting is what makes this one stand out. Rushden Lakes sits beside the River Nene and a string of lakes, and the Wildlife Trust has a visitor centre on site, so you can follow a busy session of play with a calm wander looking for ducks, swans and other water birds. It's a lovely contrast after the noise and colour indoors.

How long to stay? With no fixed session limit, you can let the kids decide. Toddlers might be done after an hour or so, while older children could happily keep going much longer. Plan a snack and drink break in the middle and you'll often find they get a second wind.

Pack socks for everyone, a change of clothes and something to drink. Weekend and holiday visits tend to be busier, so a term-time weekday morning can feel much calmer for little ones who don't love crowds.

Higham Ferrers, right next door, is a small historic market town with a pretty market square and church, and makes a peaceful place for a stroll. A short drive away, Stanwick Lakes is a big countryside spot with lakeside paths, play areas and open space for a proper run-around.

If you're making a weekend of it, Northampton is within easy reach, and the Nene Valley has plenty of walks and waterside spots to explore. All in all, a visit here can easily stretch into a whole day of play, food and fresh air without much driving at all.
